channel.title: FixMyError.net – Recently Added Errors
channel.description: Newly added developer and infrastructure error fixes on FixMyError.net.

item.title: Airflow: Broken DAG: [/opt/airflow/dags/etl.py] No module named 'x'
item.description: The DAG processor could not import the file, so the DAG vanishes from the UI and a red banner appears instead. The module is missing from the environment the scheduler or DAG processor runs in, which is often not the one you tested in: a package installed in the webserver image only, or a helper…

item.title: AWS Lambda: The runtime parameter of nodejs16.x is no longer supported
item.description: The runtime has passed its deprecation date and Lambda now blocks creating or updating functions that use it. Existing functions keep running, which is why the failure appears on an unrelated code change: the deploy touches the function configuration and the old runtime string is rejected. Bumping…

item.title: AWS Lambda: TooManyRequestsException: Rate Exceeded.
item.description: Lambda refused the invocation because the function hit its concurrency ceiling, which is the account's regional limit (1,000 by default, lower on new accounts) or the function's own reserved concurrency. It is a limit on requests running at the same moment, not requests per second, so a function…

item.title: Bundler: Your bundle only supports platforms ["arm64-darwin-23"]
item.description: Gemfile.lock records the platforms it was resolved for, and it was generated on a Mac, so the Linux CI runner or Docker image is not on the list. Bundler refuses rather than guess, because platform-specific gems such as nokogiri and ffi ship different binaries. The fix is to add the target…

item.title: C++: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.32' not found
item.description: The binary was built with a newer GCC than the machine it is running on, and it needs a libstdc++ symbol version the system library does not have. Nothing is wrong with the code: it works on the build box because that box has the newer library. It shows up when copying binaries to an older distro…

item.title: C++: error: use of deleted function
item.description: The code tries to call a function that has been explicitly deleted, and nine times out of ten that function is a copy constructor. Types such as std::unique_ptr, std::thread and std::mutex cannot be copied, so passing one by value, pushing it into a vector or capturing it in a lambda by copy…

item.title: C++: pure virtual method called, terminate called without an active exception
item.description: A pure virtual function was called through an object whose derived part does not exist at that moment. It almost always means a virtual call from a base class constructor or destructor, where the object is only the base type, or a call on an object that another thread has already started…

item.title: Cloudflare Workers: Error 1102: Worker exceeded resource limits
item.description: The Worker used more CPU time or memory than its plan allows and was stopped mid-request. CPU time counts only while your code is actually computing, so waiting on fetch() is free, but parsing a large JSON body, hashing or rendering a big page is not. A Worker that runs fine in development can hit…

item.title: CloudFront: 502 ERROR The request could not be satisfied (origin SSL failure)
item.description: CloudFront connected to the origin over HTTPS but the TLS negotiation failed, so it returned a 502 instead. The certificate on the origin must match the origin domain name configured in CloudFront, not the viewer's hostname, and must chain to a public CA. Pointing CloudFront at a load balancer's…

item.title: CloudFront: 504 ERROR The request could not be satisfied (origin timeout)
item.description: CloudFront reached for your origin and either could not open a connection or got no response in time, so the viewer sees a CloudFront error page. The origin often looks healthy when you test it directly, because the problem is on CloudFront's path: a security group or firewall that only allows…

item.title: Composer: Your lock file does not contain a compatible set of packages
item.description: composer install found that the versions pinned in composer.lock cannot run here, almost always because of the PHP version or a missing extension, not a problem with the lock file itself. The lock was generated on a machine with a newer PHP or with ext-intl or ext-gd installed, and the server or…

item.title: Gateway API: HTTPRoute Accepted=False, reason NoMatchingParent
item.description: The HTTPRoute names a Gateway in parentRefs, but no listener on that Gateway will take it, so the route is ignored and traffic never arrives. The usual causes are a sectionName or port that matches no listener, a hostname outside the listener's hostname, or a route in a namespace the listener's…

item.title: grep: Invalid range end
item.description: A bracket expression contains a range whose end sorts before its start. In POSIX brackets a backslash is literal, so [\w-.] means the range from w to a full stop, not a word character and a hyphen. Ranges like [a-Z] also depend on the locale's collation order, which is why the same command works…

item.title: gRPC: StatusCode.UNKNOWN, Exception calling application
item.description: The server's handler raised an exception it did not turn into a gRPC status, so the framework reported UNKNOWN (code 2) and the client learns nothing useful. The real traceback is in the server's log, not the client's. Other languages behave the same way: an uncaught Java exception or a panic…

item.title: gRPC: tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake
item.description: The client started a TLS handshake and the server answered in plain text, which means the client uses TLS credentials and the server, or whatever is in front of it, listens without TLS. The reverse mismatch shows as the server logging a bogus greeting or an HTTP/2 frame error. A proxy that…

item.title: gRPC: UNAVAILABLE, GOAWAY received, ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, too_many_pings
item.description: The client sent HTTP/2 keepalive pings more often than the server permits, so the server closed the connection and every call in flight failed. Client and server keepalive settings are configured separately and a client tuned to ping every few seconds will be cut off by a server using the default…

item.title: ingress-nginx: failed calling webhook "validate.nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io"
item.description: The API server tried to ask the ingress-nginx admission webhook whether your Ingress is valid and could not reach it at all, so nothing about your manifest has been judged yet. It usually means the controller pod is not running, a NetworkPolicy or private cluster firewall blocks the control plane…

item.title: ingress-nginx: host "example.com" and path "/" is already defined in ingress
item.description: The admission webhook rejected the Ingress because another Ingress, possibly in a different namespace, already claims exactly the same host and path. ingress-nginx merges every Ingress into one nginx config, so two owners for one location would be ambiguous. It often catches out a blue and green…

item.title: Keycloak: Cookie not found. Please make sure cookies are enabled
item.description: Keycloak sets a cookie when the login page loads and expects it back when the form is submitted, and it did not come back. Browsers are rarely at fault: behind a reverse proxy Keycloak often thinks it is on plain HTTP or the wrong hostname, so it issues a cookie the browser will not return…

item.title: Laravel: No application encryption key has been specified.
item.description: APP_KEY is empty in the environment Laravel actually loaded, so it cannot encrypt cookies or sessions. On a fresh clone that just means .env was never created. In production it is usually a cached config from before the key was set, or a container whose environment does not include the variable…

item.title: libvirt: Requested operation is not valid: network 'default' is not active
item.description: The VM is attached to libvirt's NAT network called default, and that network is defined but not started, so the guest cannot boot. It is not set to autostart on some distributions, and it also fails to start when dnsmasq or another DHCP server already holds its bridge address, or when a firewall…

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID: AADSTS65001: The user or administrator has not consented
item.description: The app asked for permissions that nobody in this tenant has agreed to grant it. Consent is per tenant, so an app that works in your own tenant fails in a customer's, and adding a new scope to an existing app needs fresh consent too. Many organisations block users from consenting themselves, so…

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID: AADSTS7000215: Invalid client secret provided
item.description: The client secret sent to the token endpoint is not one Entra has for that app registration. By far the most common reason is copying the secret's ID instead of its Value, since the portal shows both side by side and only reveals the value once. Expired secrets, a secret from a different app…

item.title: Pattern attribute value [a-z-_]+ is not a valid regular expression
item.description: Browsers now compile the HTML pattern attribute with the v (unicodeSets) flag, which is stricter about character classes than plain JavaScript regex. A hyphen between other characters, and unescaped characters such as ( ) [ ] { } / | inside a class, are now syntax errors. The console shows the…

item.title: PHP 8.2: Deprecated: Creation of dynamic property Foo::$bar is deprecated
item.description: Since PHP 8.2, assigning to a property that the class never declared raises a deprecation, and it is scheduled to become an error. Older code relied on setting arbitrary properties on objects, so an upgrade floods the log with these even though nothing has visibly broken. The fix is to declare the…

item.title: Proxmox: can't lock file '/var/lock/qemu-server/lock-100.conf' - got timeout
item.description: Another task still holds the lock on that VM's configuration, so the new start, stop or backup waited and gave up. The holder is usually a backup, snapshot or migration that is still running or hung, and killing the wrong process can leave the VM in a half-finished state. Check what holds the lock…

item.title: Python: re.error: global flags not at the start of the expression
item.description: An inline flag such as (?i) or (?s) appears somewhere other than the very start of the pattern. Python 3.6 to 3.10 only warned about it, and 3.11 made it an error, so code that has worked for years breaks on upgrade. It is common when patterns are built by joining strings together, each with its…

item.title: Rails: Missing encryption key to decrypt file with
item.description: Rails found config/credentials.yml.enc but has no key to open it, because config/master.key is git-ignored and RAILS_MASTER_KEY is not set. It works on the developer's laptop that ran rails new and fails on every other machine, CI job and container. Generating a new key does not help: it cannot…

item.title: Redis: MOVED 3999 10.0.0.12:6379
item.description: The node you asked does not own the hash slot for that key and is telling you which node does. A cluster-aware client follows this silently, so seeing it as an error means the client is running in standalone mode against a cluster, for example a plain connection to an ElastiCache or MemoryStore…

item.title: Ruby: warning: csv was loaded from the standard library
item.description: Ruby 3.4 moved csv, base64, bigdecimal and several other libraries out of the default gems and into bundled gems, and Ruby 3.3 warns about each one it sees you require. Under Bundler, a bundled gem is only loadable if it is in the Gemfile, so the warning today becomes cannot load such file after…

item.title: SMTP: 421 4.7.28 Our system has detected an unusual rate of unsolicited mail
item.description: Gmail is temporarily deferring mail from your IP or domain because recent volume looks like spam, judged by complaints and sudden changes in sending rate. It is a 4xx, so your server will retry, but pushing harder makes it worse. New IPs, a burst after a quiet period, and one customer on a shared…

item.title: SMTP: 535 5.7.139 Authentication unsuccessful
item.description: Microsoft 365 accepted your username and password but refused the login because authenticated SMTP submission is turned off for the tenant or the mailbox. It is off by default in newer tenants and when security defaults are enabled. The password is not wrong, so resetting it will not help; a…

item.title: SMTP: 550 5.7.1 Client host [203.0.113.5] blocked using zen.spamhaus.org
item.description: The receiving server looked up your sending IP in a DNS blocklist and found it listed, so it rejected the connection before reading the message. Your content and authentication are irrelevant here; the IP's reputation is the problem. Cloud and residential IP ranges are often listed as a whole, so…

item.title: Spark: Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits
item.description: YARN measured the whole executor process and killed it for using more physical memory than the container allowed. That is different from a Java heap OutOfMemoryError: the heap may be fine, and the excess is off-heap memory from Python workers, Arrow buffers, netty or native libraries. Raising…

item.title: Spark: org.apache.spark.shuffle.FetchFailedException: Failed to connect to
item.description: A task tried to read shuffle output from another executor and that executor was gone, so the stage has to be recomputed. The fetch failure is a symptom: look for why the executor died, which is usually memory pressure, a spot or preemptible node being reclaimed, or a long GC pause that made it…

item.title: VirtualBox: VT-x is being used by another hypervisor (VERR_VMX_IN_VMX_ROOT_MODE)
item.description: VT-x is enabled and working, but another hypervisor on a Linux host already owns it, almost always the KVM kernel module. Older VirtualBox releases cannot share VT-x, so the VM refuses to start. It commonly appears after installing an Android emulator, GNOME Boxes or virt-manager, which load KVM…

item.title: Apache: AH01630: client denied by server configuration
item.description: mod_authz_core decided the request was not allowed for that directory, so it never reached the file and the response is a 403 with nothing in the access pattern to explain it. On an upgraded server it is usually a 2.2 style Order and Allow block being ignored, or a new document root that no…

item.title: Apache: Invalid command 'Order', perhaps misspelled or defined by a module
item.description: Order, Allow and Deny moved into mod_access_compat in 2.4, so configuration written for 2.2 no longer parses unless that module is loaded. The same wording appears for any directive whose module is absent, which is why enabling the compatibility module is a stopgap and rewriting the block is the…

item.title: Dart: Bad state: Cannot add new events after calling close
item.description: A closed StreamController still exists, and something is holding the old reference and adding to it. In Flutter it is normally a controller closed in dispose while an async callback completes just afterwards, or a shared service whose controller was closed by the first widget that happened to use…

item.title: dig: ;; Truncated, retrying in TCP mode
item.description: The answer did not fit in the UDP message size the client offered, so the server set the TC bit and the client started again over TCP. The retry normally succeeds, so the visible symptom is a slow lookup, or an intermittent failure wherever a firewall permits port 53 over UDP but not TCP.

item.title: DNS: CNAME and other data (CNAME at the zone apex)
item.description: A name may hold a CNAME or it may hold other record types, never both, so a CNAME on the zone apex collides with the SOA and NS records that have to live there. The zone then fails to load, and hosted providers report it as an invalid record rather than as an error in the file.

item.title: DNS: REFUSED
item.description: The server answered and declined to do the work, which is what separates this from a timeout or NXDOMAIN. In practice it is a recursive resolver that does not serve your client address, or an authoritative server being asked about a zone it does not host, which is common once a split horizon setup…

item.title: Emscripten: Cannot call unknown function (make sure it is exported)
item.description: ccall and cwrap look the symbol up in the module at runtime, and the linker had already removed it because no C code referenced it. That is why it appears in optimised builds and not in debug ones: at -O2 dead code elimination drops any function only ever called from JavaScript.

item.title: Error 1053: The service did not respond to the start or control request
item.description: A service has about 30 seconds to report back to the service control manager, and the process either failed before doing so or spent that time on startup work. A console application installed as a service never reports at all, which is why it runs perfectly from a command prompt and times out as a…

item.title: First requests after a deploy are slow, then it settles
item.description: A freshly started process serves unoptimised code until the JIT has enough samples, with empty connection pools, empty caches and a cold page cache underneath. Rolling the deployment moves the slow requests around rather than removing them, so the graph looks like the load balancer picking bad…

item.title: Flutter: Incorrect use of ParentDataWidget
item.description: Expanded, Flexible and Positioned only mean something to one kind of parent, and the tree has one of them under something else, usually because a Container or a Padding was inserted between it and the Row. The message names both the widget and the ancestor it actually found, and the layout beneath…

item.title: Flutter: MissingPluginException: No implementation found for method
item.description: The Dart half of a plugin is present and the native half was never registered, so the method channel has nothing on the other end. A hot restart after adding the dependency is the usual cause, because plugin registration happens when the app is built and installed rather than when Dart reloads.

item.title: Flutter: Waiting for another flutter command to release the startup lock
item.description: The SDK takes a file lock while it updates its own caches, and a command killed part way through leaves that lock file behind. Nothing holds it any more, so the wait never ends, and clearing one file inside the SDK directory is all that is needed.

item.title: Homebrew: Cannot install under Rosetta 2 in ARM default prefix
item.description: The arm64 Homebrew in /opt/homebrew refuses to run in a translated process, which is what happens when the terminal itself was opened with Rosetta or a shell inherited an x86_64 environment. Two installations can coexist, one per prefix, so the message is really about which one the current shell…

item.title: JVM: pause with no GC in the log (long time to safepoint)
item.description: A safepoint stops every application thread, and the pause includes however long the slowest thread takes to reach one, which is not counted as collection time. A counted loop over a large array or a thread inside a long JNI call can hold the rest of the JVM for hundreds of milliseconds while the…

item.title: Latency spikes with khugepaged and compaction in the profile
item.description: Transparent huge pages let the kernel back a mapping with 2MB pages, but once memory is fragmented the faulting thread has to compact before it gets one, and it waits while that happens. The result is a tail latency spike on a machine with plenty of free memory, usually on a large heap process…

item.title: ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64
item.description: Compilation succeeded and the linker could not find a definition for something that was declared, so the reference survived to the link step. The architecture in the message is a red herring most of the time: a source file missing from the target, a library built for the other slice, or a C header…

item.title: macOS: "App" is damaged and can’t be opened. You should move it to the Bin
item.description: Gatekeeper is reporting a failed signature or notarisation check on a quarantined download, not a corrupted file. An app unzipped by a tool that dropped part of the bundle, modified after signing, or fetched from a mirror that never notarised it all end here, and the wording sends people to…

item.title: Name resolves with dig but not from the application
item.description: dig talks to a server directly, while the application goes through the stub resolver on 127.0.0.53, which keeps its own per link servers, search domains and cache. The two disagree after a VPN connects, when a container inherits the host resolv.conf, or while a negative answer is still cached.

item.title: nginx: [emerg] a duplicate default server for 0.0.0.0:443
item.description: Only one server block per listening address may carry default_server, and nginx refuses to start rather than choose. It nearly always follows a second site being enabled while it still has the packaged default configuration flag, or a sites-enabled directory holding two symlinks to the same file.

item.title: nginx: 1024 worker_connections are not enough
item.description: Each worker has a fixed number of connection slots and a proxied request uses two of them, one to the client and one to the upstream, so the ceiling arrives at roughly half the concurrency you expected. New connections queue or fail while CPU and memory look fine, and the message repeats once per…

item.title: Python was not found; run without arguments to install from the Microsoft Store
item.description: Windows ships app execution aliases for python.exe and python3.exe that open the Store, and they sit early enough in PATH to shadow a real installation. Anything that shells out to python hits the stub, including build scripts and node-gyp, so an interpreter you can see on disk appears to be…

item.title: Requests take a multiple of 40ms more than the work needs
item.description: Nagle's algorithm holds a small write until the previous segment is acknowledged, and the peer's delayed ACK holds that acknowledgement for up to 40ms hoping to piggyback it on data. Neither side is overloaded, they are waiting for each other, which is why the extra time is suspiciously constant…

item.title: Scala 3: `_` is no longer supported for a type wildcard, use `?`
item.description: Underscore is being reclaimed for type lambdas, so existing type wildcards have to be written with a question mark instead. It arrives as a warning during a Scala 3 upgrade and becomes an error under -source:future, and the rewrite is mechanical because only type positions changed.

item.title: Scala 3: Ambiguous given instances: both X and Y match type
item.description: Two givens of the same type are in scope with equal specificity, so the compiler refuses to choose between them. A wildcard import is the usual route in, particularly when a library ships both a default instance and a configurable one, and the ambiguity only shows up at the call site that needs it.

item.title: Scala: missing parameter type for expanded function
item.description: The compiler reached a placeholder or a lambda before it knew the expected type, so there is nothing to infer the parameter from. The cause is inference order rather than the lambda itself: a value with no declared type, an overloaded method, or a chain whose receiver type is still being worked out.

item.title: Scala: object X is not a member of package Y
item.description: The compiler resolved the package and found nothing of that name inside it, so the import fails rather than the usage. A dependency that is only on the test classpath, a stale target directory after a rename, and a package declaration that no longer matches the artefact all present identically.

item.title: Svelte 5: effect_update_depth_exceeded (Maximum update depth exceeded)
item.description: An effect wrote to state that it also reads, so running it schedules it again and Svelte gives up after a fixed number of iterations. Deriving a value inside an effect is the usual shape, and the loop often only closes once a second effect starts reading what the first one writes.

item.title: SvelteKit: Cannot access url.searchParams on a page with prerendering enabled
item.description: A prerendered page is one file written at build time, so there is no request to read a query string from. The clash usually comes from a layout: prerender was switched on once near the root and inherited by a page that filters or paginates from the URL.

item.title: SvelteKit: Cannot import $env/static/private into client-facing code
item.description: Private environment variables may only be imported by modules that never reach the browser, and the import chain from a component or a universal load function crossed that line. The offending import is often indirect: a shared helper that reads a secret gets pulled into a .svelte file by one…

item.title: SvelteKit: Cross-site POST form submissions are forbidden
item.description: SvelteKit compares the Origin header with the origin it believes it is serving and rejects the mismatch, which is its CSRF protection rather than a bug. It appears behind a proxy that does not pass the original host and protocol through, or when a form genuinely posts to another host, such as a…

item.title: The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed
item.description: The machine account password the workstation holds no longer matches the one in Active Directory, so domain logons are refused while local accounts still work. Restoring a virtual machine from a snapshot, cloning without sysprep, or leaving a machine switched off for longer than the password…

item.title: wasm-bindgen: closure invoked after being dropped
item.description: A Rust closure handed to JavaScript lives only as long as its Closure value, and letting that fall out of scope frees it while the event listener or timer still points at it. The panic therefore arrives when the callback first fires rather than where the mistake was made, which is normally a setup…

item.title: wasm-pack: crate-type must be cdylib to compile to wasm32-unknown-unknown
item.description: A Rust library defaults to the rlib crate type, which cannot be linked into a WebAssembly module, so wasm-pack stops before it ever calls the compiler. It usually means the crate was started with cargo new rather than from the wasm template, or that a new workspace member inherited the default.

item.title: Web3: could not detect network (event="noNetwork", code=NETWORK_ERROR)
item.description: ethers asks the endpoint for its chain id before it will do anything else, and that call failed, so the provider never finished starting. A wrong URL is only one cause: a missing key in the path, a rate limited key, a browser CORS rejection and an http endpoint on an https page all look identical…

item.title: Web3: max code size exceeded when deploying a contract
item.description: EIP-170 caps deployed runtime code at 24576 bytes and the deployment is rejected once the compiled contract passes it. The growth is usually incidental rather than a single large addition: long revert strings, many public functions and inlined library code all count, and building with the…

item.title: Web3: Transaction reverted without a reason string
item.description: The contract used require without a message, tripped an assert, ran out of gas inside a nested call, or the address has no code for that selector, so there is no string to decode. The tooling reports the absence rather than the cause, which is why the same call against a live node returns only a…

item.title: Web3: transaction underpriced
item.description: The node rejected the transaction before it entered the pool because the fee offered is below the minimum it will accept, which is local policy rather than a consensus rule. It differs from the replacement case: nothing is pending for that nonce, the fee is simply under this node’s floor or under…

item.title: WebAssembly: Import #0 module="env" error: module is not an object or function
item.description: The module declares imports and the importObject handed to instantiate has no property for that namespace, so the engine gives up before linking anything. It is the normal outcome of loading an Emscripten or WASI build with a bare instantiate call, because those toolchains expect their own…

item.title: Windows: A required privilege is not held by the client (0x80070522)
item.description: Creating a symbolic link needs SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege, which standard accounts do not hold, so git checkouts, npm installs and archive extractions that contain links fail with something that reads like a file permission problem. Developer Mode grants the privilege without making the whole…

item.title: Xcode: building for 'iOS-simulator', but linking in object file built for 'iOS'
item.description: A dependency in the project carries a device slice only, and the simulator build cannot link it even though both are arm64 on Apple silicon. It turns up with an old fat framework or a binary pod published before XCFrameworks existed, and excluding arm64 hides it at the cost of breaking the…

item.title: Ansible: Failed to import the required Python library (docker) on host
item.description: Modules run on the target with the interpreter Ansible discovered there, so a library installed on the control node, or into a different virtualenv, is invisible to them. The message names the interpreter it used, and that path is the part worth reading before installing anything again.

item.title: Ansible: No inventory was parsed, only implicit localhost is available
item.description: Ansible found no usable inventory, so every host pattern matches nothing and the run ends with "skipping: no hosts matched" and an exit code of zero. A file that exists but fails to parse produces the same warning as one that is missing, which is why a YAML inventory with the wrong shape looks…

item.title: Connections hang or reset with ListenOverflows increasing
item.description: The kernel finished the handshake but the application was too slow to call accept(), so the completed connection queue filled and further connections were dropped silently. Clients see a stall and then a timeout or a reset, and nothing appears in the application log because the connection never…

item.title: DMARC: dmarc=fail (p=reject) in Authentication-Results
item.description: SPF or DKIM passed on its own but neither aligned with the domain in the From header, and alignment is what DMARC checks. This is why mail sent through a third party can pass SPF against the provider domain and still be rejected as your domain.

item.title: Elixir: (DBConnection.ConnectionError) tcp recv: closed
item.description: The database closed a pooled socket that Ecto still believed was usable, so the checkout succeeded and the query died on the wire. The usual culprit is something between the application and the database with an idle timeout: a pgbouncer server_idle_timeout, an RDS proxy, or a cloud load balancer…

item.title: Elixir: (MatchError) no match of right hand side value: {:error, :enoent}
item.description: A pattern match assumed the happy path and the function returned the error tuple instead, so the process crashed at the assignment rather than at the failure. The value in the message is the whole answer: it names both what went wrong and which call produced it.

item.title: Elixir: protocol String.Chars not implemented for %{} of type Map
item.description: String interpolation calls to_string/1, and only a few types implement it: maps, lists, tuples and structs do not. The failure is at runtime rather than compile time, so it usually appears in an error path or a log line that only runs when something else has already gone wrong.

item.title: Go: error parsing regexp: invalid or unsupported Perl syntax: (?!
item.description: Go uses RE2, which has no backtracking and therefore no lookahead, no lookbehind and no backreferences. That is a deliberate guarantee of linear time matching rather than a missing feature, so the pattern has to be restructured instead of escaped.

item.title: gRPC: connection error: desc = transport: Error while dialing
item.description: The channel could not open a TCP or TLS connection, so the RPC fails with UNAVAILABLE and this wrapped cause. Because Dial is lazy in the Go client, the mistake surfaces on the first call rather than at construction, which makes it look like a request problem rather than a target or credentials one.

item.title: High iowait: load average climbing while the CPU sits idle
item.description: Linux counts tasks in uninterruptible sleep towards the load average, so processes blocked on a disk or an NFS mount push load into double figures on a box that is 95 per cent idle. The number sends people hunting for a CPU problem that does not exist, when the queue is in front of a device.

item.title: ingress-nginx: Service does not have any active Endpoint
item.description: The controller resolved the Ingress to a Service but the Service selects no ready Pods, so it serves the default backend and returns 404 instead of routing. The Ingress and the Service both look correct in kubectl get, because the gap is between the Service selector and the Pod labels or the…

item.title: ingress-nginx: upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)
item.description: The controller gave up waiting for the backend and returned 504 after its own timeout, which defaults to 60 seconds and is set on the controller, not on the application. A long report or an upload that works when called directly against the Service will fail through the Ingress for exactly this…

item.title: Ingress: ADDRESS column stays empty and the host never resolves
item.description: kubectl get ingress shows no address because no controller has claimed the object, so nothing ever programmes a load balancer or writes the status back. The Ingress itself is valid, which is why it is accepted without complaint and then does nothing at all.

item.title: Java: PatternSyntaxException: Illegal repetition
item.description: A brace appears where the engine expects a quantifier, so a literal { in the pattern is read as the start of {n,m} and rejected. It shows up most often when a template placeholder such as {name} is passed straight to Pattern.compile or to String.replaceAll.

item.title: libvirt: Failed to connect socket to /var/run/libvirt/libvirt-sock
item.description: virsh connected to the session daemon rather than the system one, or the user is not in the group that owns the socket. The same command works under sudo, which is the clue: it is a permission and URI problem, not a daemon that failed to start.

item.title: log4j2: ERROR StatusLogger No Log4j 2 configuration file found
item.description: Log4j 2 could not find log4j2.xml on the classpath and fell back to logging errors only to the console, which is why the application starts but INFO and DEBUG never appear. In a packaged jar the file is usually present in the source tree and missing from the artefact, not absent from the repository.

item.title: Machine crawls with CPU idle: swap thrashing (si/so in vmstat)
item.description: Once the working set no longer fits in RAM the kernel evicts pages that are about to be needed again, so every fault costs a disk read and throughput collapses long before memory is fully exhausted. The giveaway is sustained si and so columns in vmstat, not the free figure, which looks healthy…

item.title: Nginx: proxy_cache never stores anything (X-Cache-Status: MISS)
item.description: Nginx honours the upstream response headers, so a Set-Cookie, a Cache-Control of private or no-store, or an unset Expires stops it caching even though proxy_cache_path is configured correctly. Every request is then a MISS, and the cache directory stays empty rather than filling up and evicting.

item.title: Python: logging.basicConfig() has no effect and nothing is logged
item.description: basicConfig only does anything when the root logger has no handlers yet, so it is a silent no operation if any import or framework configured logging first. The second trap is the level: the default is WARNING, so info() and debug() are dropped even when the handler is correct.

item.title: Python: re.error: look-behind requires fixed-width pattern
item.description: The standard re module only implements lookbehind when every alternative is the same known length, so a quantifier or an alternation of different widths inside (?<=...) is rejected at compile time. The pattern is valid in .NET and in the third party regex module, which is why one copied from a…

item.title: sbt: Conflicting cross-version suffixes in: org.scala-lang.modules
item.description: Two dependencies pulled in the same library built for different Scala versions, for example scala-xml _2.12 and _2.13 in one classpath. It usually follows a Scala upgrade where one dependency was written with a single per cent rather than a double, so its suffix was pinned by hand and never moved.

item.title: Scala: could not find implicit value for parameter
item.description: The compiler could not supply an implicit argument, usually because the instance exists but is not in scope, or because the type it was defined for is slightly different from the one being summoned. Libraries such as Circe and Play JSON report a missing Encoder or Format this way when the real…

item.title: Scala: recursive value x needs type
item.description: A definition refers to its own name on the right hand side, so the compiler cannot infer the type it is in the middle of inferring. It is almost never real recursion: the usual cause is a val that shadows something with the same name, such as a constructor parameter reused as a field.

item.title: Scala: warning: match may not be exhaustive
item.description: The compiler proved a case is missing from a match on a sealed type, and with fatal warnings enabled the build stops. It is worth reading rather than silencing: the same warning is how a new subtype added elsewhere in the codebase tells you every match that has not been updated.

item.title: SLF4J: Failed to load class org.slf4j.impl.StaticLoggerBinder
item.description: The SLF4J API is on the classpath with no binding behind it, so every log call is discarded through the no operation logger and the application runs in silence. With SLF4J 2.x the wording changes to "No SLF4J providers were found", but the cause is the same missing implementation.

item.title: SMTP: 451 4.7.1 Greylisted, please try again later
item.description: The receiving server deliberately rejected a first delivery attempt from an unknown sender triple and expects a retry, which real mail servers do and most spam software does not. It is a temporary failure, so the only bug is in senders that treat any 4xx as final and drop the message.

item.title: SMTP: 552 5.3.4 Message size exceeds fixed maximum message size
item.description: The message was larger than the receiving server accepts, and the limit applies after MIME encoding, which inflates attachments by roughly a third. A 20 MB file therefore fails against a 25 MB limit, and the rejection happens at the smallest limit along the path, not the one you configured.

item.title: VirtualBox: Kernel driver not installed (rc=-1908)
item.description: The vboxdrv module is missing or refused to load, which normally follows a kernel upgrade that left the DKMS build behind. On a machine with Secure Boot the module builds correctly and is then rejected at load time because it is unsigned, which is a different failure with the same message.

item.title: VirtualBox: VERR_NEM_VM_CREATE_FAILED / raw-mode is unavailable
item.description: Something else on Windows already owns the hardware virtualisation extensions, so VirtualBox is pushed onto the Hyper-V layer or fails to create the VM at all. WSL 2, Docker Desktop, Windows Sandbox and memory integrity all switch Hyper-V on, usually without the user connecting that to the VM that…

item.title: wasm-bindgen: recursive use of an object detected
item.description: A Rust method holding a mutable borrow of a struct called into JavaScript, and that JavaScript called back into the same object before the first call returned. Rust borrow rules are enforced at runtime across the boundary, so what would be a compile error inside Rust becomes this exception in the…

item.title: Web3: already known / ALREADY_EXISTS when sending a transaction
item.description: The node already holds a transaction with this exact hash in its pool, so the resend is rejected rather than duplicated. It normally means a retry loop signed the identical payload again, or the same nonce was submitted to two nodes behind one RPC endpoint.

item.title: Web3: cannot estimate gas; transaction may fail or may require manual gas limit
item.description: The node ran the transaction against current state and it reverted, so no gas figure could be produced. The wording suggests a gas problem but the cause is almost always the call itself: a missing token approval, a paused contract, or a require that fails for this sender.

item.title: Web3: query returned more than 10000 results (eth_getLogs)
item.description: The RPC provider caps how much a single log query may return or how many blocks it may span, and the limit is per provider rather than part of the JSON-RPC spec. The same code works against a local node and fails on a hosted endpoint, usually at the point where an indexer starts from the contract…

item.title: WebAssembly: LinkError: import object field is not a Function
item.description: Instantiation failed because the import object handed to the module does not match what the module declares it needs: a missing property, a nested namespace that is undefined, or a value where a function was expected. The module name comes first in the error, so env.abort means the module asked…

item.title: WebAssembly: RuntimeError: table index is out of bounds
item.description: An indirect call used a function pointer that is not in the module table, which normally means a callback was passed to C or C++ without being registered, or the table was built too small at link time. The pointer looks valid on the Rust or C side because it is just an integer.

item.title: Container CPU throttling: nr_throttled rising in cpu.stat
item.description: A CPU limit is enforced as a quota per 100ms period, so a process that spends its quota early is stopped until the period ends. Average utilisation looks comfortable while p99 latency spikes, which is why this gets blamed on the database or the network long before anyone reads cpu.stat.

item.title: Dart: type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'String' in type cast
item.description: A cast met a null at runtime, and with sound null safety the failure lands on the cast rather than on first use. Nearly every occurrence is JSON decoding: `json['name'] as String` passes in testing and throws the first time the server omits the field or sends null for it.

item.title: docker: could not select device driver with capabilities: [[gpu]]
item.description: --gpus needs the NVIDIA container toolkit registered as a runtime with the daemon; having the driver installed on the host is not enough. It also appears after an upgrade, because a package that rewrites /etc/docker/daemon.json can drop the runtime entry while leaving everything else working.

item.title: Elixir: (KeyError) key :name not found in: %{"name" => "ada"}
item.description: Dot access and `Map.fetch!/2` raise rather than returning nil when a key is missing, and the usual cause is string keys where atom keys were expected. A map decoded from JSON has `"name"`, not `:name`, and the two are different keys in the same map.

item.title: Elixir: function Foo.bar/1 is undefined (module Foo is not available)
item.description: The module was never loaded, which in practice means a misspelled alias, a file outside the compile paths, or a dependency that is in `mix.exs` but whose application was never started. Note the wording: if the module existed and only the function were wrong, the message would name the module as…

item.title: Elixir: protocol Enumerable not implemented for nil of type Atom
item.description: Something handed `Enum` a nil where a list was expected, and nil has no Enumerable implementation. The real fault is upstream: an Ecto association that was never preloaded, a `Map.get` that missed, or a function whose error branch returns nil instead of an empty list.

item.title: Flutter: No Material widget found
item.description: Widgets such as TextField, ListTile and InkWell paint ink on the nearest Material ancestor and throw when there is none above them. It appears inside a showDialog builder, a custom PageRoute or a widget test that pumps the widget on its own, because those trees start below the Scaffold.

item.title: Flutter: setState() or markNeedsBuild() called during build
item.description: Something changed state while the framework was already building the tree, so it is being asked to rebuild a widget it has not finished with. The usual cause is work that belongs in initState or in a callback being run directly inside build: notifying a provider, starting navigation, or showing a…

item.title: Flutter: Vertical viewport was given unbounded height
item.description: A scrolling widget was placed somewhere with no height to fill, typically inside a Column or another scrollable, and both want to size themselves to their children. The message names the inner ListView, but the constraint that is missing comes from the parent.

item.title: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded
item.description: The JVM spent over 98 percent of recent time collecting and recovered less than 2 percent of the heap, so it stopped rather than crawling on. The heap need not be full: a cache holding strong references keeps everything reachable, and the collector works harder each cycle for less return.

item.title: journalctl: No journal files were found
item.description: journald stores logs in memory when /var/log/journal does not exist, so everything is discarded at reboot. The service was logging normally, but the evidence for the crash you came to investigate went away with the machine, which is why the directory matters more than any retention setting.

item.title: kubectl top: error: Metrics API not available
item.description: kubectl top and every horizontal pod autoscaler read from metrics-server, which no upstream cluster installs by default. The same message appears when it is installed but never becomes ready, usually because it cannot verify the kubelet's self signed serving certificate.

item.title: logrotate: skipping because parent directory has insecure permissions
item.description: logrotate refuses to rotate a file in a directory that is group or world writable, because doing that work as root would be an escalation path. Nothing else breaks, so rotation just stops and the disk fills a few weeks later, long after the message scrolled past in the timer output.

item.title: Phoenix: (Phoenix.Router.NoRouteError) no route found for GET /api/users
item.description: No clause in the router matched, so Phoenix raises rather than quietly returning 404 in development. The path is usually right and the verb or the scope is not: a link issuing GET for a delete route, or a route written with the prefix that its enclosing `scope` already adds.

item.title: Python: re.error: bad escape \d at position 0
item.description: The replacement argument of re.sub is not a pattern. It understands only group references such as \1 and \g plus the standard string escapes, so a regex fragment or a Windows path pasted into it raises. The same text is perfectly valid as the pattern argument, which makes the message look wrong.

item.title: Regex: test() returns false every other call with the /g flag
item.description: A regex with the g or y flag keeps lastIndex between calls, so test() resumes from where the previous match ended and alternates between true and false on the same input. It is worst when the regex is a module level constant shared by every request the process handles.

item.title: Scala: NoClassDefFoundError: scala/collection/IterableOnce
item.description: A jar built for a different Scala version is on the classpath. Scala is only binary compatible within a minor version, so a 2.12 artifact loaded by a 2.13 runtime looks for classes that were moved or renamed. It compiles, because the missing class is only resolved when the code first runs.

item.title: Scala: type mismatch; found: Unit, required: String
item.description: The last expression in the block is an assignment or a `for` loop, both of which evaluate to Unit, so the block returns nothing useful. It reads as a compiler mistake because the value the author meant to return is two lines up, discarded by whatever came after it.

item.title: Spark: org.apache.spark.SparkException: Task not serializable
item.description: A closure sent to the executors dragged an unserialisable object along with it. Referencing one field of an enclosing class captures the whole instance, so a lambda that only needs a string can pull in a database connection, a logger or the SparkSession itself.

item.title: Svelte 5: `$effect` can only be used inside an effect
item.description: Effects have to be created while a component is initialising, so calling `$effect` from a click handler, a `setTimeout` callback or an async function after an `await` throws. The rule usually catches an attempt to start a subscription in response to an event rather than declaring it up front and…

item.title: Svelte 5: `$props()` can only be used at the top level of components
item.description: Runes are compiled away rather than called, so `$props()` has to appear exactly once as the initialiser of a top level declaration in a component's instance script. Destructuring it inside a function, a condition or a `.svelte.js` module looks like an ordinary call but fails to compile.

item.title: Svelte 5: State referenced in its own scope will never update
item.description: Reading a `$state` variable into a plain `const`, or passing it to a function, copies the value at that moment instead of keeping the reactive reference. The component still updates when the state changes, but your copy does not, so the page shows a stale number and nothing in the code looks wrong.

item.title: Svelte 5: Updating state inside a derived is forbidden
item.description: A `$derived` expression re-runs whenever its inputs change, so writing state from inside one would feed the change back into itself. It almost always appears after a migration, where a `$:` statement that both computed a value and assigned to something else was converted mechanically into a single…

item.title: SvelteKit: Cannot prerender pages with actions
item.description: Prerendering happens at build time and produces a static file, while a form action needs a server when the request arrives, so one route cannot do both. It usually surfaces because `prerender = true` was set on a root layout months ago and a page underneath it has just gained a form.

item.title: Web3: gas required exceeds allowance (0)
item.description: The node simulated the transaction and found the sender cannot cover it, so the allowance it reports is the gas the balance affords, often zero. Despite the wording it is rarely a gas limit problem: the account is empty, or it is the wrong account, or the wrong chain is selected in the wallet.

item.title: Web3: max fee per gas less than block base fee
item.description: The node rejected the transaction because its maxFeePerGas is below the base fee of the next block. Base fee moves by up to 12.5 percent per block, so a fee read a few seconds earlier, or a value hard coded in a script, is stale by the time the transaction is submitted.

item.title: Web3: missing revert data in call exception (CALL_EXCEPTION)
item.description: The call failed without a reason string, which usually means there is no contract at that address on this chain rather than a failed require. A deployment address from a different network, a proxy that was never initialised, or an ABI that does not match the deployed bytecode all produce it.

item.title: WebAssembly: null function or function signature mismatch
item.description: An indirect call went through the function table and found an empty slot, or a function whose type does not match the call site. In Emscripten builds it is a C function pointer cast to the wrong signature, or a JavaScript callback registered with a signature string that does not match what it is…

item.title: WebAssembly: RuntimeError: unreachable executed
item.description: The module reached an `unreachable` instruction, which compilers emit wherever the program traps: a Rust panic, an assertion, `abort()`, or a C++ exception in a build compiled without exception support. The JavaScript stack shows a wasm frame and nothing else, so the useful detail is whatever the…

item.title: WebAssembly: SharedArrayBuffer is not defined
item.description: Threaded builds need shared memory, and browsers only expose SharedArrayBuffer to cross origin isolated pages. The module works on localhost and fails on the deployed site, because isolation comes from response headers that the dev server sets and the CDN in front of production does not.

item.title: Android: Manifest merger failed with multiple errors, see logs
item.description: Gradle merges your manifest with every library manifest, and two of them disagree: usually a minSdkVersion lower than a dependency allows, or the same attribute declared with different values. The build log line above this one names the attribute; the merged result and its blame report say which…

item.title: Android: SDK location not found. Define a valid SDK location
item.description: Gradle looks for sdk.dir in local.properties, then for the ANDROID_HOME environment variable. local.properties is machine specific and is git ignored by every Android template, so this is almost always a build running somewhere the SDK path was never set: CI, a container, or a freshly cloned…

item.title: Ansible: The conditional check 'result.rc == 0' failed
item.description: The when expression could not be evaluated, usually because the variable it names does not exist on this host: the registering task was skipped, ran on a different host, or the play failed before reaching it. The message continues with the Jinja error, and 'dict object' has no attribute is the…

item.title: Ansible: you must install the sshpass program
item.description: OpenSSH refuses to read a password from anything but a terminal, so Ansible shells out to sshpass whenever a connection or become password is supplied rather than a key. The program is not a dependency of Ansible and is missing from most container images, which is why a playbook that runs on a…

item.title: Apollo Server: POST body missing, invalid Content-Type
item.description: Apollo Server 4 does not parse request bodies itself, so the Express integration needs express.json() mounted before it. The other half of the cases is a client or proxy that sends no content type header, since anything other than application/json or application/graphql-response+json is refused.

item.title: C++: relocation R_X86_64_32S can not be used when making a shared object
item.description: A shared library must be loadable at any address, so every object in it needs position independent code. The object triggering this is nearly always from a static library built without -fPIC and then linked into a .so, which is why the advice to recompile applies to that dependency rather than to…

item.title: C++: undefined reference to `vtable for X'
item.description: This is not a missing call to the named function. The compiler emits a class's vtable alongside the definition of its first non inline virtual function, so if that function is declared and never defined, or its translation unit is missing from the link, the vtable is never emitted. A virtual…

item.title: CMake Error: Could not find a package configuration file provided by X
item.description: find_package looked for a config file the library installs, XConfig.cmake or x-config.cmake, and no directory it searched had one. The library being present in the system is not enough: the runtime package often ships without the config file, which lives in the development package or in a prefix…

item.title: Dart: LateInitializationError: Field 'x' has not been initialized
item.description: late promises the compiler that a non nullable field will hold a value before anything reads it, and that promise was broken. Reading it during initState before the assignment, or on a code path where the assignment is conditional, throws at the point of the read rather than where the field was…

item.title: Ecto: connection not available and request was dropped from queue
item.description: Every connection in the pool was busy for longer than queue_target allowed, so DBConnection gave up rather than queueing indefinitely. Raising pool_size is the reflex and rarely the cure: the pool is usually held by a handful of slow queries, or by processes doing HTTP calls inside a transaction.

item.title: Elixir: (FunctionClauseError) no function clause matching
item.description: Every clause of the function was tried and none matched the arguments, either on the pattern or on a guard. Elixir prints the attempted clauses and the arguments it was given, so the useful comparison is between the two: a nil where a map was expected, a string key where an atom was expected, or a…

item.title: Flutter: A RenderFlex overflowed by 42 pixels on the right
item.description: A Row or Column laid out children that want more space than the parent offered, so the excess is painted as the yellow and black stripes. The number is the overflow, not the required width, and the fix depends on intent: a child that should shrink needs Flexible, one that should scroll needs a…

item.title: Flutter: setState() called after dispose()
item.description: An asynchronous callback finished after its widget left the tree, so the State it wants to update no longer exists. The await is the giveaway: the widget can be disposed while the request is in flight, which is why the crash only appears when the user navigates away quickly or the network is slow.

item.title: go: cannot find main module; see 'go help modules'
item.description: The command was run outside any module: there is no go.mod in the working directory or any parent. Since Go 1.16 module mode is the default, so a repository that once built from GOPATH, or a Dockerfile that copies sources without go.mod, fails here rather than falling back.

item.title: Go: panic: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3
item.description: Go slices are zero indexed, so the valid indexes stop one short of len. The message gives both numbers, and when the index is exactly the length the loop ran one iteration too far; when it is far larger the index came from data, not from the loop, and needs validating before use.

item.title: go: updates to go.mod needed; to update it: go mod tidy
item.description: Go stopped editing go.mod as a side effect of build commands in 1.16, so a missing or stale requirement is now reported instead of quietly added. It usually appears in CI first, because a local run had already written the change into go.mod that nobody committed.

item.title: GraphQL: Cannot use GraphQLSchema from another module or realm
item.description: Two copies of the graphql package are installed, so the schema was built with one and validated by the other. graphql-js checks identity with instanceof, which fails across copies even when the versions match, and the message blames the schema rather than the duplicated dependency.

item.title: GraphQL: Variable "$id" of required type "ID!" was not provided
item.description: Validation rejected the request before any resolver ran, because a non null variable was declared in the document but missing from the variables map. Sending null is not the same as sending nothing for a non null type, and a key that is present but undefined is dropped by JSON.stringify, which is…

item.title: Ingress: configuration-snippet annotation cannot be used
item.description: ingress-nginx 1.9 turned allow-snippet-annotations off by default after snippets were shown to let any namespace inject configuration into the shared nginx process. Manifests that worked for years are rejected by the admission webhook at apply time, so the failure appears during an upgrade rather…

item.title: Java: Cannot invoke "String.length()" because "s" is null
item.description: This is a helpful NullPointerException message, on by default since Java 15, and it names the exact expression that was null rather than just the line. When the name reads as or a synthetic name, the class was compiled without debug information, so recompiling with -g restores the real variable…

item.title: Java: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
item.description: The heap could not satisfy an allocation after a full collection. Raising -Xmx only helps when the working set genuinely grew; if the cause is a leak, a bigger heap moves the crash later and makes the pauses worse. A heap dump taken at the moment of failure tells the two apart.

item.title: Java: NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class X
item.description: This is not a missing class. The class was found, its static initialiser ran and threw, and every later use reports this instead. The real exception appears only the first time, often much earlier in the log, and is usually a missing config value, a failing static block or an incompatible…

item.title: Jest: Exceeded timeout of 5000 ms for a test
item.description: The test returned a promise that never settled within the limit. A slow network call is the obvious cause, but the common one is a promise that cannot settle: a missing await, a done callback never called, or fake timers installed so the timer the code is waiting on never advances.

item.title: Jest: Your test suite must contain at least one test.
item.description: A file matched the test pattern but declared no test. Helper files living beside the tests are the usual reason, because the default pattern picks up everything inside a __tests__ directory, not only files named .test.js. A file where every test is skipped or filtered out fails the same way.

item.title: Memcached: SERVER_ERROR object too large for cache
item.description: The item exceeded the maximum item size, one megabyte by default, so it was refused rather than stored. Because most clients treat a failed set as a cache miss, the symptom is usually a page that is mysteriously slow rather than an error: every request recomputes the same oversized value.

item.title: React Native: Unable to load script. Make sure you're running Metro
item.description: The debug build fetches its JavaScript bundle from Metro at runtime, and the device could not reach it. On a physical Android device localhost means the phone itself, so the port has to be forwarded over adb; on a release build the message instead means the bundle was never packaged into the app.

item.title: Redis: NOSCRIPT No matching script. Please use EVAL.
item.description: EVALSHA runs a script the server has already cached by hash, and that cache is not persisted. A restart, a failover to a replica that never saw the script, or a SCRIPT FLUSH empties it, so a client that only ever sends the hash starts failing until it loads the body again.

item.title: Regex: nothing to repeat at position 0
item.description: A quantifier appeared with nothing before it to repeat, so the pattern is invalid rather than merely wrong. It is almost always a pattern built at runtime: user input interpolated into a regex, or a string that already contained a plus or asterisk meant literally.

item.title: Rust: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
item.description: unwrap says the value is definitely there, and it was not, so the thread panicked at that line. The message names the file and column of the unwrap, not of the code that produced the None, which is why the interesting frame is usually further down the backtrace.

item.title: Rust: cannot borrow `*self` as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable
item.description: The immutable borrow is usually hidden in an argument: self.push(self.len()) borrows self to evaluate the argument while the method call already holds a mutable borrow. Borrows end at their last use under NLL, so the fix is nearly always to finish the read before starting the write rather than to…

item.title: Rust: recursive type has infinite size (E0072)
item.description: A struct or enum that contains itself by value would need infinite space, because the compiler lays out every field inline. The fix is not to remove the recursion but to put a pointer in the cycle, which has a known size and moves the child onto the heap.

item.title: Scala: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: scala.Predef$.refArrayOps
item.description: The code compiled against one version of the Scala library and is running against another. Scala guarantees binary compatibility only within a minor series, so a dependency published for 2.12 pulled into a 2.13 build, or two libraries built against different minor versions, produces a method that…

item.title: Spring Boot: required a bean of type 'X' that could not be found
item.description: Component scanning starts at the package of the class annotated with @SpringBootApplication and covers only that package and below. A bean in a sibling package, or one whose @Component annotation is missing, is never registered, which is why the same class works in a test that declares it…

item.title: Svelte 5: `export let` is not allowed in runes mode, use `$props()` instead
item.description: A component is in runes mode, where props arrive through $props() rather than exported let bindings. Runes mode is chosen per component: using any rune anywhere in the file switches it, so adding a single $state to a legacy component makes every remaining export let in it illegal.

item.title: SvelteKit: Data returned from `load` is not serializable
item.description: Data from a server load function is serialised so the browser can hydrate with it, and the serialiser handles plain objects, arrays, Date, Map, Set and a few more, but not class instances. ORM rows are the usual offender: a Prisma Decimal, a Mongo ObjectId or a Mongoose document looks like a plain…

item.title: systemd-journald: Suppressed 1234 messages from /system.slice/app.service
item.description: journald rate limits each service, discarding the rest of a burst rather than slowing the writer. The lines are gone, not delayed, which makes it look as though the application stopped logging exactly when it got interesting: incidents produce bursts, and the burst is what gets dropped.

item.title: Tokio: Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime
item.description: Something called block_on on a thread that is already driving the async runtime, which would deadlock the worker, so Tokio panics instead. The call is usually not yours: a blocking client such as reqwest::blocking, or a library helper that hides block_on, used from inside an async function.

item.title: TypeScript: 'error' is of type 'unknown' (TS18046)
item.description: Since TypeScript 4.4, useUnknownInCatchVariables (part of strict) types the catch binding as unknown rather than any, because JavaScript lets you throw anything, not just an Error. The code did not change; the compiler now insists you prove what you caught before reading a property off it.

item.title: TypeScript: Module can only be default-imported using the 'esModuleInterop' flag
item.description: The package is CommonJS and sets module.exports directly, so it has no ES default export to bind. esModuleInterop makes the compiler emit a helper that wraps such a module, which is why the same import works in a bundler that already does this and fails in tsc.

item.title: TypeScript: Option 'module' must be set to 'NodeNext'
item.description: moduleResolution and module are not independent: the Node16 and NodeNext resolution modes read package.json exports and the type field, and only the matching module setting emits code that agrees with them. Copying a moduleResolution line from a bundler config into a Node project is the usual way…

item.title: TypeScript: Parameter 'x' implicitly has an 'any' type (TS7006)
item.description: Under noImplicitAny, which strict turns on, TypeScript refuses a parameter it cannot infer. Callback parameters are normally inferred from the function they are passed to, so seeing this on a callback means the surrounding value is untyped: an untyped library, a variable annotated as any, or a…

item.title: TypeScript: Two different types with this name exist, but they are unrelated
item.description: Two copies of the same type package are installed at different paths, usually @types/react or @types/node pulled in at two versions by different dependencies. The types are structurally identical but nominally distinct, so a value from one tree cannot be assigned to a parameter typed by the other.

item.title: Vitest: ReferenceError: document is not defined
item.description: Vitest runs in Node by default, where there is no DOM. The component test needs a browser like environment declared, either for the whole project or per file. Unlike Jest, Vitest does not bundle jsdom, so the package has to be installed as well as configured.

item.title: WebAssembly: Cannot enlarge memory arrays
item.description: The module asked for more linear memory than it was built to have. Emscripten fixes the heap at INITIAL_MEMORY unless memory growth was enabled at link time, so this is a build setting rather than a browser limit, and the same binary fails identically in Node and in every browser.

item.title: Xcode: Sandbox: rsync.samba deny(1) file-write-create
item.description: Xcode 15 turned on user script sandboxing for new projects, and a build phase tried to write outside the files it declared. The phase is usually not one you wrote: CocoaPods copies frameworks and resources with rsync, and Flutter and React Native ship similar scripts, so the failure appears after…

item.title: .NET: The framework 'Microsoft.NETCore.App', version '8.0.0' was not found
item.description: The published application is framework dependent and the machine has no matching runtime. Roll forward will pick a newer patch of the same major version but never a different major, so an app built for 8.0 will not start on a box that only has 9.0 installed.

item.title: Angular: NG0100: ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError
item.description: A binding produced one value during change detection and a different one when Angular verified the pass in development mode. It normally means a parent reads state that a child mutates while initialising, so the check runs before the value has settled. Production builds skip the verification…

item.title: Apollo Client: Missing field 'x' while writing result to the cache
item.description: The normalised cache stores objects by id and typename, and the response left out a field the cache needed, usually because one query selects a subset that a fragment elsewhere expects. It is only a warning, but the later read returns incomplete data and refetches, which looks like a caching bug…

item.title: ASP.NET Core: Unable to resolve service for type while activating
item.description: The container was asked for a dependency nobody registered, so the controller or hosted service could not be constructed. The rest of the message names the type that needed it, which is the quickest way to tell whether the missing registration is yours or belongs to a library whose AddSomething…

item.title: AWS ECS: CannotPullContainerError, pull image manifest has been retried
item.description: The task could not fetch its image, and the reason is far more often networking than permissions: a task in a private subnet with no NAT gateway and no VPC endpoints cannot reach ECR at all. A task in a public subnet still needs assignPublicIp turned on before it has a route out.

item.title: AWS: The security token included in the request is expired
item.description: The temporary credentials issued by STS have passed their expiry, which is one hour by default for an assumed role. A long build, a laptop resumed from sleep with a stale cache, or a clock that has drifted by more than a few minutes all produce it even though credentials are clearly present.

item.title: bash: warning: setlocale: LC_ALL: cannot change locale
item.description: SSH forwards the client's locale variables and the server has no such locale generated, so every login prints the warning and programs fall back to the C locale. The fallback is the part that matters: sorting order, date parsing and Unicode handling all change underneath you.

item.title: Cargo: Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache
item.description: Cargo takes an exclusive lock on its home directory so two builds cannot corrupt the registry. The message is harmless while another build is genuinely running, but a lock left behind by a killed process, or a cache mounted read only in a container, makes the build wait for ever instead of failing.

item.title: Django: Forbidden (403) CSRF verification failed. Request aborted.
item.description: Django rejected the POST because the CSRF token or the request Origin did not match the session. Behind a reverse proxy the cause is usually not a missing token at all: since Django 4.0 the Origin header is compared against CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, so a site served over HTTPS whose proxy forwards the…

item.title: Docker: image's platform (linux/amd64) does not match the detected host
item.description: The image has no build for the host architecture, so Docker Desktop runs it under emulation on Apple Silicon. It is a warning rather than an error, but emulated containers are slow and some binaries die with an illegal instruction, which is the failure people actually end up debugging.

item.title: docker: invalid reference format
item.description: Docker could not parse the image name. The usual causes are an uppercase letter in the repository part, a shell variable that expanded to nothing, or an unquoted path in a volume flag containing a space, which pushes the rest of the command into the position where the image name should be.

item.title: DOMException: play() failed because the user didn't interact with the document
item.description: Browsers block audible autoplay until the page has received a user gesture. play() returns a promise that rejects rather than throwing, so an unhandled rejection in the console is the only clue and the video simply sits there. Muted playback is still allowed, which is why the same code works on…

item.title: EF Core: another instance with the same key value is already being tracked
item.description: The change tracker already holds an entity with that primary key and Attach or Update tried to add a second copy. It normally follows a tracked read earlier in the request, then an update built from the request body. The first query is the cause even though the second call is what throws.

item.title: git: You have divergent branches and need to specify how to reconcile them
item.description: Local and remote have both moved on, and since Git 2.27 pull refuses to guess between merging and rebasing. The hint offers three settings without recommending one, which is why it is so often answered with a global config that then surprises everyone in the next repository.
